code: library(mfrmr) calibration_responses <- read.csv(   "calibration-responses.csv", colClasses = "character", na.strings = "",   check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM" ) gpcm_fit <- fit_mfrm(   calibration_responses,   person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"), score = "Score",   model = "GPCM", method = "MML",   step_facet = "Rater", slope_facet = "Criterion",   rating_min = 0, rating_max = 2, category_policy = "preserve",   mml_integration = "adaptive", quad_points = 31,   maxit = 400, reltol = 1e-10 ) summary(gpcm_fit, profile = "fit", detail = "brief") draft <- extract_mfrm_calibration(   gpcm_fit, calibration_id = "rubric-calibration",   source_fit_id = "training-cohort", scoring_quad_points = 141 ) review_mfrm_calibration(draft) calibration <- update(status = "frozen", update(status = "validated", draft)) save_mfrm_calibration(calibration, "gpcm-calibration.rds") library(mfrmr) # A later session needs only this file and the new response rows. calibration <- load_mfrm_calibration("gpcm-calibration.rds") new_responses <- read.csv(   "new-responses.csv", colClasses = "character", na.strings = "",   check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM" ) scores <- score_mfrm_calibration(   calibration, new_responses, missing_response = "omit" ) score_review <- summary(scores) score_review score_review$review score_review$settings$score_integration_review plot(scores, type = "interval", preset = "publication", top_n = Inf)  # Keep full-precision scores and every Person's disposition, including those # without scores. The complete object supports later review and plotting. write.csv(scores$estimates, "person-scores.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "") write.csv(scores$person_dispositions, "person-review.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "") saveRDS(scores, "scored-cohort.rds") retained <- scores$settings$retained_prior_identity  # Sensitivity analysis on the same calibration scale, not a new population fit. alternative <- score_mfrm_calibration(   calibration, new_responses, missing_response = "omit",   scoring_prior = list(mean = retained$mean + 0.5, sd = retained$sd * 1.25) ) summary(alternative) library(mfrmr)  calibration <- load_mfrm_calibration("reviewed-calibration.rds") new_rows <- read.csv(   "new-responses.csv",   colClasses = "character",   na.strings = "",   check.names = FALSE,   fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM" ) scores <- score_mfrm_calibration(calibration, new_rows) print(scores) plot(scores, type = "interval", preset = "publication") write.csv(scores$estimates, "person-scores.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Available estimates range from -1.22 to 1.06 #> logits. Criterion measures ranged from #> -0.34 to 0.22 logits (M = 0.00, SD = 0.30). #>  #> Fit and precision. #> Overall mean-square fit was within the 0.5-1.5 screening band (infit MnSq = 0.87, outfit #> MnSq = 0.86). This band is the package's review convention; published mean-square #> guidelines differ, and band position is screening evidence rather than a model-validity #> decision. MnSq outside [0.5, 1.5]: 18 of 57 classified elements flagged; 0 of 57 elements #> unclassified. Largest misfit signals among 57 elements with complete paired statistics: #> Person:P022 (|ZSTD| = 2.88); Person:P026 (|ZSTD| = 2.84); Criterion:Content (|ZSTD| = #> 2.27). Criterion reliability = 0.87 (separation = 2.56). Person reliability = 0.66 #> (separation = 1.41). Rater reliability = 0.68 (separation = 1.45). Separation reliability #> describes differences among facet locations relative to their estimation errors. High #> Person values indicate distinguishable abilities; high rater values indicate #> distinguishable severities, not inter-rater agreement. Low rater values can also reflect #> imprecision and do not establish agreement. The index does not test every rater pair or #> quantify the practical size of severity differences. Reliability, separation and Strata are #> approximate compatibility indices using marginal SEs; joint-information SEs do not validate #> this variance decomposition. They do not account for covariance among estimates. EAP-based #> separation is not posterior-variance EAP reliability. Model and fit-adjusted values are #> companion indices, not confidence limits. Strata describes hypothetical distinguishable #> strata, not discovered groups. Facet heterogeneity chi-square summaries use diagonal SE #> weights, not full-covariance joint tests. The Person row uses EAP measures with posterior #> SDs, which yields a conservative summary that is not numerically comparable to JMLE-based #> person reliability from FACETS. Inter-rater agreement for Rater is reported separately from #> separation reliability. Diagnostics match scores within Person and all remaining non-rater #> facets; each compared pair contributes one opportunity per matched context. The denominator #> is 138 matched-context opportunities across rater pairs, not a count of independent people. #> 6 of 15 candidate rater pairs have matched scores. Observed exact agreement = 0.39; #> observed adjacent agreement (absolute score difference at most 1, including exact matches) #> = 0.86; model-expected exact agreement = 0.35. The model-expected baseline uses fitted #> category probabilities with calibration fixed; it is not chance agreement or an inferential #> test. It assumes conditional independence at the saved Person point score (EAP for MML), #> rather than integrating over the Person posterior. These descriptive summaries do not #> classify rater quality or establish fairness. Element-level 95% approximate intervals #> (Normal approximation) accompany 57 of 57 estimates; 57 of 57 estimates have intervals #> eligible for primary reporting. #>  #> Residual structure. #> Overall categories: 0 flagged among 4 classified; 0 of 4 unavailable. Step/scale groups: 0 #> flagged among 1 classified; 0 of 1 unavailable. Facet levels: 1 flagged among 9 classified; #> 0 of 9 unavailable. Level pairs: 1 flagged among 9 classified; 0 of 9 unavailable. Expected #> counts condition on the same responses through Person posteriors, with fitted calibration #> held fixed. Residual scales omit cross-response covariance and calibration-parameter #> uncertainty; thresholds are descriptive, not calibrated tests. Strict marginal screening #> gives an overall RMSD of 0.01, overall max |standardized residual| = 0.43. The largest #> strict marginal cell involved Criterion: Content | Cat 4 (standardized residual = -1.53, #> proportion difference = -0.06). Strict pairwise local-dependence follow-up flagged 1 level #> pair(s) under the latent-integrated agreement screen.       matrix(c(0, cumsum(fit$calibration$steps)), order, 3, byrow = TRUE)     prob <- exp(logw - apply(logw, 1, max))     prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)     conditional <- rep(1, nrow(patterns))     for (block in split(seq_along(membership), membership)) {       block_prob <- matrix(1, order, nrow(patterns))       for (j in block) {         block_prob <- block_prob * prob[, patterns[, j] + 1L, drop = FALSE]       }       conditional <- conditional * as.vector(crossprod(rule$weights, block_prob))     }     answer <- answer + rule$weights[h] * conditional   }   answer }  evaluate_parallel_plan <- function(fit, membership) {   stopifnot(inherits(fit, "mfrm_testlet"),     length(fit$input$columns$facets) == 0L,     identical(as.numeric(fit$input$score_levels), 0:2 + 0),     length(membership) == 4L, !anyNA(membership))   patterns <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:2), 4)))   data <- data.frame(Person = rep(sprintf("Y%02d", 1:81), each = 4),     Task = rep(membership, 81), Score = as.vector(t(patterns)))   scores <- predict(fit, data, quad_points = 61)   stopifnot(identical(scores$table$Person, sprintf("Y%02d", 1:81)),             all(scores$table$Status == "available_conditional"))   low <- pattern_mass(fit, membership, patterns, 61)   probability <- pattern_mass(fit, membership, patterns, 121)   tab <- scores$table   v <- fit$calibration$person_variance   expected_variance <- sum(probability * tab$ConditionalSD^2)   stopifnot(abs(sum(probability) - 1) < 1e-8,     max(abs(low - probability)) < 1e-8,     abs(sum(probability * tab$Estimate)) < 1e-7,     abs(sum(probability * (tab$ConditionalSD^2 + tab$Estimate^2)) - v) < 1e-7)   list(scores = scores, probability = probability, patterns = patterns,     membership = membership, summary = data.frame(       RMSPosteriorSD = sqrt(expected_variance),       ModelImpliedEAPReliability = 1 - expected_variance / v)) }

what: Save a figure with its values and notes
title: mfrmr Visual Diagnostics
text: Saving PNG loses underlying values interpretation notes. Save complete returned object well. example uses temporary filename; choose project filename keep beyond R session. Keep rubric alongside plot: labels illustrative labels used earlier, wording mfrmr inferred scores. Use actual rubric wording.  supported Wright-map conversion, redraw saved values without refitting recalculating uncertainty: ggplot2 imported mfrmr, plot() as_ggplot() return ggplot objects directly (as_ggplot() also converts saved 0.2.x mfrm_plot_data objects). Save fit matching diagnostics want choose different analysis view later. plot guide distinguishes dedicated figure views table-based component views.
code: figure_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") figure_record <- list(plot = wright,   rubric = c(`1` = "Beginning", `2` = "Developing", `3` = "Secure", `4` = "Advanced")) saveRDS(figure_record, figure_file) saved_record <- readRDS(figure_file) saved_figure <- saved_record$plot saved_record$rubric #>            1            2            3            4  #>  "Beginning" "Developing"     "Secure"   "Advanced" print(saved_figure) identical(plot_data(saved_figure, "locations"), plot_data(wright, "locations")) #> [1] TRUE as_ggplot(saved_figure)

what: Set an appearance once for several plots
title: mfrmr Visual Diagnostics
text: Use options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "monochrome") set common default development version. example restores previous option ends: choices "standard", "publication", "compact" "monochrome". Explicit preset wins option; omitting retains "standard". Explicit preset = NULL also selects package default. Remove session setting options(mfrmr.plot_preset = NULL). supported as_ggplot(saved) conversion uses saved preset, whereas new plot(fit, ...) call uses current option. Set option script use explicit arguments reproduce appearance another session. applies common preset controls, including category, coverage network report plots. Extended-model plots separate palette controls retain settings. change estimates, confidence levels, screening thresholds user’s global ggplot theme.
code: local({   old <- options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "monochrome")   on.exit(options(old))   saved <- plot(fit, type = "ccc", draw = FALSE)   special <- plot(fit, type = "ccc", preset = "publication", draw = FALSE)   c(     session_default = plot_data(saved, "preset"),     explicit_override = plot_data(special, "preset")   ) }) #>   session_default explicit_override  #>      "monochrome"     "publication"

code: library(mfrmr)  # One row per rating: 48 persons x 4 raters x 4 criteria, scores 1--4. ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") for (v in c("Person", "Rater", "Criterion")) ratings[[v]] <- factor(ratings[[v]]) ratings$Rating <- ordered(ratings$Score, levels = 1:4) persons <- data.frame(Person = levels(ratings$Person)) stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ratings[c("Person", "Rater", "Criterion")]),   all(with(ratings, table(Person, Rater, Criterion)) == 1L))  # 1. mfrmr: adjacent-category models with fixed rater/criterion effects. # ~1 estimates the mean and variance of the normal person distribution. fit_native <- function(model, ...) {   fit_mfrm(ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),     score = "Score", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,     model = model, method = "MML", category_policy = "preserve",     population_formula = ~1, person_data = persons, person_id = "Person",     quad_points = 61, ...) } mfrmr_fits <- list(   RSM = fit_native("RSM"),   PCM = fit_native("PCM", step_facet = "Criterion"),   GPCM = fit_native("GPCM", step_facet = "Criterion", slope_facet = "Criterion") ) # This table records likelihoods; it is not a recommendation to choose GPCM. sapply(mfrmr_fits, function(x) as.numeric(logLik(x))) summary(mfrmr_fits$GPCM)  # 2. ordinal: cumulative models with the same additive facet structure. # Positive fixed coefficients mean higher ratings (lower severity/difficulty). # The Person random intercept has mean 0 and an estimated variance. ordinal_logit <- ordinal::clmm(   Rating ~ Rater + Criterion + (1 | Person), data = ratings,   link = "logit", nAGQ = 15, Hess = TRUE,   contrasts = list(Rater = "contr.treatment", Criterion = "contr.treatment") ) ordinal_probit <- ordinal::clmm(   Rating ~ Rater + Criterion + (1 | Person), data = ratings,   link = "probit", nAGQ = 15, Hess = TRUE,   contrasts = list(Rater = "contr.treatment", Criterion = "contr.treatment") ) summary(ordinal_logit)  # 3. lavaan: the corresponding cumulative-probit measurement structure. # Reshape to one row per person; keep every rater-by-criterion response. cells <- unique(ratings[c("Rater", "Criterion")]) cells <- cells[order(cells$Rater, cells$Criterion), ] r <- as.integer(cells$Rater) j <- as.integer(cells$Criterion) cells$Indicator <- paste0("y", r, "_", j) ratings$Indicator <- cells$Indicator[match(   paste(ratings$Rater, ratings$Criterion), paste(cells$Rater, cells$Criterion))] wide <- reshape(ratings[c("Person", "Indicator", "Score")],   idvar = "Person", timevar = "Indicator", direction = "wide") names(wide) <- sub("^Score\\.", "", names(wide)) items <- cells$Indicator intercepts <- paste0("i", r, "_", j)  # Unit loadings and unit residual variances fix the probit response scale. # Shared cutpoints + additive intercepts reproduce the fixed-facet structure. # Rater 1 / Criterion 1 is the reference cell; ability has mean 0. syntax <- c(   paste("Ability =~", paste(paste0("1*", items), collapse = " + ")),   "Ability ~~ variance*Ability", "Ability ~ 0*1",   paste(items, "~~", paste0("1*", items)),   paste(items, "| cut1*t1 + cut2*t2 + cut3*t3"),   paste(items, "~", paste0(ifelse(r == 1 & j == 1, "0", intercepts), "*1")) ) for (i in which(r > 1 & j > 1)) {   syntax <- c(syntax, paste0(intercepts[i], " == i", r[i], "_1 + i1_", j[i])) } syntax <- paste(syntax, collapse = "\n") cat(syntax) # Inspect the actual constraints before fitting. lavaan_probit <- lavaan::cfa(syntax, data = wide, ordered = items,   estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "theta") stopifnot(lavaan::lavInspect(lavaan_probit, "converged")) lavaan::parameterEstimates(lavaan_probit)  # This fits the same cumulative-probit response structure as ordinal_probit, # using WLSMV rather than marginal ML. Estimates and SEs need not coincide. # It is not an adjacent-logit RSM, PCM or GPCM. sapply(c("mfrmr", "ordinal", "lavaan"), function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p))) sessionInfo() # Run the data setup above first. Dichotomization is used only to demonstrate # the binary special case; it discards information from the original ratings. binary <- ratings binary$Score01 <- as.integer(binary$Score >= 3) binary$Rating01 <- ordered(binary$Score01, levels = 0:1) binary_mfrmr <- fit_mfrm(binary, person = "Person",   facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"), score = "Score01",   rating_min = 0, rating_max = 1, model = "RSM", method = "MML",   category_policy = "preserve", population_formula = ~1,   person_data = persons, person_id = "Person", quad_points = 61) binary_ordinal <- ordinal::clmm(   Rating01 ~ Rater + Criterion + (1 | Person), data = binary,   link = "logit", nAGQ = 15, Hess = TRUE,   contrasts = list(Rater = "contr.treatment", Criterion = "contr.treatment")) c(mfrmr = as.numeric(logLik(binary_mfrmr)),   ordinal = as.numeric(logLik(binary_ordinal))) # Compare likelihoods rather than raw locations: mfrmr centres facets, # while this ordinal fit uses reference levels and a zero-mean random effect. # Person EAP means and random-effect conditional modes are also different. library(ggplot2)  eta <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 301L) adjacent <- exp(outer(eta, 0:2) - pmax(0, 2 * eta)) adjacent <- adjacent / rowSums(adjacent) cumulative <- function(cdf, cuts) {   lower <- cdf(cuts[1L] - eta)   upper <- cdf(cuts[2L] - eta)   cbind(lower, upper - lower, 1 - upper) } logit <- cumulative(plogis, qlogis(c(1 / 3, 2 / 3))) probit <- cumulative(pnorm, qnorm(c(1 / 3, 2 / 3))) probabilities <- list(   "mfrmr (RSM): adjacent logit" = adjacent,   "Ordinal mixed model: cumulative logit" = logit,   "Ordinal CFA: cumulative probit" = probit )  # Verify the displayed probabilities and the defining link equations. center <- which.min(abs(eta)) for (p in probabilities) {   stopifnot(all(is.finite(p)), all(p >= 0), all(p <= 1),     max(abs(rowSums(p) - 1)) < 1e-14,     max(abs(p[center, ] - 1 / 3)) < 1e-14,     all(diff(drop(p %*% (0:2))) > 0)) } stopifnot(   max(abs(log(adjacent[, 2] / adjacent[, 1]) - eta)) < 1e-13,   max(abs(log(adjacent[, 3] / adjacent[, 2]) - eta)) < 1e-13,   max(abs(qlogis(logit[, 1]) - (qlogis(1 / 3) - eta))) < 1e-12,   max(abs(qlogis(rowSums(logit[, 1:2])) - (qlogis(2 / 3) - eta))) < 1e-12,   max(abs(qnorm(probit[, 1]) - (qnorm(1 / 3) - eta))) < 1e-12,   max(abs(qnorm(rowSums(probit[, 1:2])) - (qnorm(2 / 3) - eta))) < 1e-12 ) curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(probabilities), function(model) {   data.frame(Predictor = rep(eta, 3L),     Probability = as.vector(probabilities[[model]]),     Category = factor(rep(0:2, each = length(eta)),       labels = paste("Score", 0:2)), Model = model) })) curves$Model <- factor(curves$Model, levels = names(probabilities))  figure <- ggplot(curves, aes(Predictor, Probability,     colour = Model, linetype = Model)) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dotted") +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.95) +   geom_point(data = curves[curves$Predictor == 0 & curves$Model == names(probabilities)[1L], ],     colour = "#222222", size = 2.4, show.legend = FALSE) +   facet_wrap(~Category, ncol = 1) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#B35A00", "#007E68"),     labels = c("mfrmr (RSM)", "ordinal (logit)", "lavaan (probit)")) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed", "longdash"),     labels = c("mfrmr (RSM)", "ordinal (logit)", "lavaan (probit)")) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3, expand = expansion(mult = 0.015)) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1),     labels = c("0", "1/3", "2/3", "1")) +   labs(x = "Predictor (within-model units)", y = "Category probability") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 16, base_family = "sans") +   theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",     legend.text = element_text(size = 12),     legend.title = element_blank(),     strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),     panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),     panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),     panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),     plot.margin = margin(8, 12, 8, 8))  # Save in the working directory, then display the same figure. ggsave("model-families.svg", figure, device = svglite::svglite,   width = 7.2, height = 8.3, bg = "white") figure

No population model was requested; MML used an unconditional normal person distribution.  # Extract the ordinary data frame for further formatting or export tbl$table #>       Facet Levels MeanEstimate SDEstimate MinEstimate MaxEstimate Span #> 1 Criterion      3            0        0.3       -0.34        0.22 0.57 #> 2     Rater      6            0        0.4       -0.61        0.41 1.02 # This table summarizes facets; use as.data.frame(fit) for individual estimates # Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below. # example("summary.apa_table", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core. # For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm. example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr")) fit <- example_fit$fit tbl <- apa_table(fit, which = "summary") summary(tbl) } # } # Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below. # example("plot.apa_table", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core. # For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm. example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr")) fit <- example_fit$fit tbl <- apa_table(fit, which = "summary") p <- plot(tbl, draw = FALSE) p2 <- plot(tbl, type = "first_numeric", draw = FALSE) if (interactive()) {   plot(     tbl,     type = "numeric_profile",     main = "APA Numeric Profile (Customized)",     palette = c(numeric_profile = "#2b8cbe", grid = "#d9d9d9"),     label_angle = 45   ) } } # }

How much would G improve by changing from six to twelve tasks? change <- confint(d, parm = "G", reference = 1, assumption = "normal") change[, c("Tasks", "ReferenceCount", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] # The same planning question for absolute dependability; coverage is approximate. phi_change <- confint(d, parm = "Phi", reference = 1, assumption = "normal") phi_change[, c("Tasks", "ReferenceCount", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] attr(phi_change, "monte_carlo")$endpoint_bands # Sampling uncertainty in measurement SEM, rather than in G or Phi. sem_ci <- confint(d, parm = "AbsoluteSEM", assumption = "normal") sem_ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Method", "Status")] sem_change <- confint(d, parm = "RelativeSEM", reference = 1,                       assumption = "normal") sem_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] sem_plot <- plot(d, type = "sem", metric = "AbsoluteSEM", intervals = TRUE,                  assumption = "normal", draw = FALSE) plot_data(sem_plot, "notes") # Different raters serve each task; retain three raters per task. data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested", package = "mfrmr") gn <- mfrm_g_study(mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested,   c("Content", "Organization"), nesting = c(Rater = "Task")) dn <- mfrm_d_study(gn,   data.frame(Raters = 3, Tasks = c(6, 12))) nested_change <- confint(dn, parm = "G", reference = 1, assumption = "normal") nested_change[, c("Raters", "Tasks", "ReferenceCount", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper")] attr(nested_change, "nesting_context") # Incomplete one-facet ratings: relative SEM without likelihood fitting. observed <- tasks[(tasks$Person + tasks$Task) %% 3 != 0, ] sparse_g <- mfrm_g_study(observed, "V", rater = NULL, method = "minque0") sparse_d <- mfrm_d_study(sparse_g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12))) residual_sem <- confint(sparse_d, parm = "RelativeSEM",   method = "residual_contrast", assumption = "normal") residual_sem[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] residual_change <- confint(sparse_d, parm = "RelativeSEM", reference = 1,   method = "residual_contrast", assumption = "normal") residual_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper")] # Relative G also uses Person variation; normal Person effects are required. spectral_g <- confint(sparse_d, method = "spectral_f", assumption = "normal") spectral_g[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] spectral_change <- confint(sparse_d, method = "spectral_f", reference = 1,   assumption = "normal") spectral_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper")] # A separate experimental REML model can address G/Phi or absolute SEM. if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("minqa", quietly = TRUE)) {   profile_ci <- confint(sparse_d, method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")   profile_ci[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "Validation")]   attr(profile_ci, "notes")   # Uncertainty in absolute measurement SEM, in score units.   profile_sem <- confint(sparse_d, parm = "AbsoluteSEM",                          method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")   plot(sparse_d, type = "sem", metric = "AbsoluteSEM", intervals = profile_sem,        draw = FALSE)   # How much does doubling the task count change G?   profile_change <- confint(sparse_d, reference = 1,     method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")   profile_change[, c("Tasks", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper")]   attr(profile_change, "base_interval")   plot(profile_change, draw = FALSE) } # Start with the default two-crossed-facet approximation on bundled data. data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed", package = "mfrmr") crossed <- mfrm_g_study(mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed,   c("Content", "Organization")) future <- mfrm_d_study(crossed,   data.frame(Raters = c(2, 4), Tasks = c(6, 12)),   weights = c(Content = .5, Organization = .5)) crossed_ci <- confint(future, parm = "Phi", assumption = "normal") crossed_ci[, c("Raters", "Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper",                "FormulaComplete", "Status")] attr(crossed_ci, "notes") # The score method remains an explicit experimental comparison for G. score_ci <- confint(future, method = "score", assumption = "normal") score_ci[, c("Scenario", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Empty", "Status")] # Vary task counts within each rater count to obtain planning-curve ribbons. curve_plans <- mfrm_d_study(crossed,   expand.grid(Raters = c(2, 4), Tasks = c(3, 6, 12)),   weights = c(Content = .5, Organization = .5)) score_curve <- plot(curve_plans, metric = "G", intervals = TRUE,   method = "score", assumption = "normal", draw = FALSE) plot_data(score_curve, "notes") if (requireNamespace("lpSolve", quietly = TRUE)) {   comparison <- confint(future, parm = "Phi", assumption = "normal",     method = c("mls", "approximate_f", "mean_square_region"))   comparison[, c("Scenario", "Method", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]   figure <- plot(comparison, draw = FALSE)   plot_data(figure, "notes")   if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) as_ggplot(figure)   # General nested comparison: both counts change, with eighteen ratings.   general_nested <- mfrm_d_study(gn,     data.frame(Raters = c(3, 2, 6), Tasks = c(6, 9, 3)))   nested_region <- confint(general_nested, parm = "Phi", reference = 1,     method = "mean_square_region", assumption = "normal")   nested_region[, c("Raters", "Tasks", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]   attr(nested_region, "reference")$counts } } # } # Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below. # example("summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Published synthetic data, not empirical speech-contest records. ratings <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr")) g <- mfrm_g_study(ratings, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL) d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)),   weights = c(V = .5, W = .5)) # Compare dependability and measurement error under the normal-effects model. s <- summary(d, intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal") print(s, digits = 3) # One row per plan for absolute dependability; the complete table is retained. subset(s$table, Metric == "Phi",   select = c(Tasks, Estimate, Lower, Upper, Status)) # Reuse an interval for a curve, with no interval calculation. p <- plot(d, metric = "Phi", intervals = s$intervals$Phi, draw = FALSE) plot_data(p, "notes") } # } # Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below. # example("plot.mfrm_dstudy_intervals", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ tasks <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr")) g <- mfrm_g_study(tasks, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL) d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12))) ci <- confint(d, assumption = "normal") p <- plot(ci, draw = FALSE) plot_data(p, "notes") if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) as_ggplot(p) } # }

no new G-study is fitted. confint(g, parm = "Person", score = "V", assumption = "normal", level = .90) # Covariance between the two observed scores, retaining its sign. covariance_ci <- confint(g, score = c("V", "W"), method = "gci",   assumption = "normal") covariance_ci[, c("Source", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] attr(covariance_ci, "monte_carlo")$endpoint_bands # Incomplete ratings: a residual-only interval without likelihood fitting. observed <- tasks[(tasks$Person + tasks$Task) %% 3 != 0, ] sparse_g <- mfrm_g_study(observed, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL,                                    method = "minque0") residual_ci <- confint(sparse_g, parm = "Residual", score = "V",   method = "residual_contrast", assumption = "normal") residual_ci[, c("Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] attr(residual_ci, "residual_projection")$df # A separate experimental REML model can address other components. if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("minqa", quietly = TRUE)) {   profile_ci <- confint(sparse_g, score = "V", method = "reml_profile",                         assumption = "normal")   profile_ci[, c("Source", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "SEStatus")]   attr(profile_ci, "notes")   # Two scores require a joint model; this is covariance, not correlation.   joint_ci <- confint(sparse_g, parm = "Person", score = c("V", "W"),                       method = "reml_profile", assumption = "normal")   joint_ci[, c("Source", "Estimate", "IntervalCenter", "Lower", "Upper", "Validation")] } } # } # Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below. # example("vcov.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed", package = "mfrmr") ratings <- mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed # Complete balanced ratings: compute both targets directly. g <- mfrm_g_study(ratings, c("Content", "Organization"),                             method = "anova") sampling <- vcov(g, score = "Content", assumption = "normal") attr(sampling, "summary") # Component estimates and their sampling SEs. attr(sampling, "notes") # Uncertainty in the covariance between two criteria, by source. cross_score <- vcov(g, score = c("Content", "Organization"),                     assumption = "normal") attr(cross_score, "summary")  # Incomplete assignments also work, but their moment calculation is longer. # These saved results use the same ratings with rows 1, 8 and 23 omitted. # Omitted ratings are absent observations, never zero scores. incomplete <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "gstudy-sampling.rds",                                   package = "mfrmr", mustWork = TRUE)) incomplete$study$design attr(incomplete$variance, "summary") attr(incomplete$covariance, "summary") attr(incomplete$covariance, "notes") # To repeat the full incomplete-data calculation: # source(system.file("examples", "gstudy-sampling.R", package = "mfrmr")) # incomplete <- gstudy_sampling_example() } # }

code: # Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed. # example("confint.mfrm_fair_average", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ d <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") # Calibrate the observed ratings with ordinary joint maximum likelihood. f <- fit_mfrm(d, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",   method = "JML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",   optimizer = "BFGS", maxit = 500, reltol = 1e-11) # The bundled example's rubric is 1--4; declare it independently of sample extrema. # Every Person is evaluated against these same Rater-Criterion cells. plan <- unique(d[c("Rater", "Criterion")]) fair <- fair_average_table(f, reference_plan = plan) head(fair$reference_scores) # Expected average, in internal score units. # Two replications exercise the API only; they cannot qualify coverage. # Explicit experimental generator; points and every refit remain ordinary JML. ci <- confint(fair, parm = c("P001", "P002"), nsim = 2, seed = 71,   generator_method = "jeffreys",   contrasts = matrix(c(1, -1), 1,     dimnames = list("P001 minus P002", c("P001", "P002")))) summary(ci) # Read Status and Available alongside the limits. attr(ci, "trials") # Includes unresolved refits and their reasons. attr(ci, "monte_carlo") # Infinite enclosures expose the two-draw tail uncertainty. plot(ci, draw = FALSE) # Saved plotting data, including the cautions. # Deterministic local approximation to the same expected-score target: delta <- confint(fair, parm = c("P001", "P002"), method = "delta") delta[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Available", "CIEligible")] attr(delta, "covariance") # Includes the covariance between Persons. # Conservative alternative with explicit observed/unobserved plan support: bounded <- confint(fair, parm = c("P001", "P002"), method = "bounded") bounded[, c("Target", "Estimate", "DesignEstimate", "CI_Lower", "CI_Upper", "Informative")] attr(bounded, "support") # Check how much of the plan was actually observed. } # } # Continue the confint.mfrm_fair_average() example: # plot(ci) # p <- plot(ci, draw = FALSE) # plot_data(p, "notes") # Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed. # example("fair_average_table", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(mfrmr)  # Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational. # For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm. example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr")) fit <- example_fit$fit  # Use the diagnostics saved with this fit diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics  # Compare observed person means with model-based scores on a common reference fair <- fair_average_table(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics, facets = "Person",                            reference = "mean", label_style = "native") head(fair$raw_by_facet$Person[, c("Level", "ObservedAverage", "FairM")]) # FairM uses the mean reference for the other facets; it is in score units # It is a conditional model prediction, not a guarantee of fairness  # Fit the same synthetic ratings by JML to illustrate total-score extrapolation toy <- load_mfrmr_data(example_fit$dataset) jml <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "JML") extreme_report <- fair_average_table(jml, xtreme = .3, xtreme_method = "facets") head(extreme_report$raw_by_facet$Person[, c("Level", "PrimaryMeasure",      "Measure", "MeasureBasis", "ModelSE", "MeasureSEBasis")]) # ModelSE describes the adjusted total when MeasureBasis says extrapolation } # }

example("mfrm_d_study", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ plot(d, type = "sem") # Without weights, report the original scores without creating a composite. individual <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12))) plot(individual, score = "V")  # Explicit GENOVA convention for a single observed score. g_one <- mfrm_g_study(tasks, "V", rater = NULL) d_ems <- mfrm_d_study(g_one, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)),   negative_components = "genova_ems") summary(d_ems) ci_ems <- confint(d_ems, assumption = "normal") # Adjusted point and original-source population interval have separate bases. ci_ems[, c("Estimate", "IntervalEstimate", "Lower", "Upper", "IntervalBasis")] d_ems$effective_components # Compare with d_ems$gstudy$components. plot(d_ems, metric = "G", intervals = ci_ems) # Original-source population bounds.  # Compare weight choices on the same task-count scenarios. weights <- cbind(Equal = c(V = 0.5, W = 0.5),   W_focus = c(V = 0.2, W = 0.8), Difference = c(V = -1, W = 1)) alternatives <- mfrm_d_study(g,   data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)), weights = weights) summary(alternatives) # Original scores plus all three named composites. plot(alternatives, composite = "Equal") plot(alternatives, composite = "Difference", type = "sem") # Choose weights for the intended interpretation, not solely for higher G. } # code: # Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed. # example("mfrm_facet_intervals", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",   model = "RSM", method = "MML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,   category_policy = "preserve") intervals <- mfrm_facet_intervals(fit, "Rater", method = "sandwich") summary(intervals)[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper",   "Status", "CIEligible", "InferenceReview")] # Keep all rows: a missing interval does not imply a missing point. plot(intervals) # Crosses mark retained estimates with unavailable intervals.  # Compare two selected raters, rather than each rater against the origin. # Here choose the first two example labels; prespecify your own comparison. raters <- unique(as.character(ratings$Rater)) contrast <- matrix(0, 1, length(raters), dimnames = list(   paste(raters[1], "minus", raters[2]), raters)) contrast[1, 1:2] <- c(1, -1) difference <- mfrm_facet_intervals(fit, "Rater", contrasts = contrast) summary(difference)[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] # With the default negative rater sign, a positive contrast means the first # rater is more severe. Units are native logits. An interval containing zero # leaves the direction uncertain; it does not establish equivalence.  # Estimate the population SD in this same model before standardizing. # Even an intercept-only population model needs one row per person. persons <- unique(ratings["Person"]) population_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"),   "Score", model = "RSM", method = "MML", population_formula = ~ 1,   person_data = persons, person_id = "Person",   rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve", quad_points = 61) standardized <- mfrm_facet_intervals(population_fit, "Rater",   contrasts = contrast, scale = "standardized") summary(standardized) # Estimate is now in fitted ability-population SD units; its delta-method # interval includes uncertainty in that SD. It is not a Wald z statistic.  # CML estimates the native contrast without an ability distribution. if (requireNamespace("lpSolve", quietly = TRUE)) {   cml_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",     model = "RSM", method = "CML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,     category_policy = "preserve")   cml_ci <- mfrm_facet_intervals(cml_fit, "Rater", contrasts = contrast)   summary(cml_ci)   apa_table(cml_ci)   file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") # Choose a lasting path for your analysis   saveRDS(cml_ci, file)   saved <- readRDS(file)   summary(saved) # Same conditional-information result, without refitting   # Use plot(saved) for a figure; ordinary mfrm_results() does not accept CML. } } # }

At six tasks, W - V has G = 0.30000 and Phi = 0.24116 (Appendix E).  # An illustrative incomplete assignment roster, not a missingness model. sparse <- tasks[(tasks$Person + tasks$Task) %% 3 != 0, ] sparse$V[1] <- NA_real_ # One assigned score is additionally unrecorded. g_sparse <- mfrm_g_study(sparse, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL,   method = "minque0", missing = "omit") g_sparse$data_usage g_sparse$estimation$component_support g_sparse$component_diagnostics # Explicit future COMPLETE designs, not reliability of the sparse roster. d_sparse <- mfrm_d_study(g_sparse,   data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)), weights = c(V = -1, W = 1)) d_sparse$coefficients # Read metric status and ComponentPSD separately.  # Existing continuous-score example; rename columns to show role mapping. data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed", package = "mfrmr") ratings <- mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed names(ratings)[names(ratings) == "Rater"] <- "Assessor" names(ratings)[names(ratings) == "Task"] <- "Session" head(ratings) # Two score columns for each Person-Assessor-Session cell. # Here sessions represent exchangeable assessments, without a time trend. g <- mfrm_g_study(ratings, c("Content", "Organization"),   facets = c(Rater = "Assessor", Occasion = "Session")) g$components$Person g$component_diagnostics d <- mfrm_d_study(g,   design_grid = data.frame(Rater = c(2, 4), Occasion = c(3, 3)),   weights = c(Content = 0.6, Organization = 0.4)) d$coefficients # Difference-score dependability, when subtraction is meaningful on these scales. difference <- mfrm_d_study(g,   weights = c(Content = 1, Organization = -1)) difference$coefficients  # Rater-only planning for one occasion; no generalization across occasions. one_session <- ratings[ratings$Session == 1, ] g_rater <- mfrm_g_study(one_session, c("Content", "Organization"),   rater = "Assessor", task = NULL) d_rater <- mfrm_d_study(g_rater, data.frame(Raters = c(1, 2, 4))) plot(d_rater, score = "Content")  # Different rater teams for different tasks; the same Persons and scores. data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested", package = "mfrmr") nested <- mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested head(nested) # R1 in Task 1 is a different rater from R1 in Task 2. g_nested <- mfrm_g_study(nested, c("Content", "Organization"),   nesting = c(Rater = "Task")) g_nested$design$child_counts # Three raters per task; eighteen in total. g_nested$component_diagnostics d_nested <- mfrm_d_study(g_nested,   expand.grid(Raters = c(2, 3), Tasks = c(4, 6)),   weights = c(Content = 0.6, Organization = 0.4)) summary(d_nested) plot(d_nested, x_var = "Raters") # Raters on the axis means raters PER TASK. plot(d_nested, x_var = "Tasks", type = "sem") } # }

"simulation" "network" return advanced design-review rows. "response_time" returns descriptive response-time QC rows. "models" compares fixed-facet, shared-rater Person-specific testlet workflows, including distinct prediction reporting boundaries. "feedback" distinguishes fixed-rater uncertainty, unexpected rating patterns, shared-rater uncertainty, observed agreement, centrality, criterion-referenced accuracy screening accuracy known truth. "features", "imputation" "gtheory" show exploratory attributes, assigned-score multiple imputation observed-score G/D-study workflows, including table, plot saving routes. "facets", "conquest", "r" return user-pathway rows people arriving workflows. ... Optional sub-scope filter arguments specialist matrices: scope = "intervals": optional category ("", "visual", "table", "reporting", "fit", "bias", "linking", "gpcm", "equivalence", "hierarchical", "shrinkage"). scope = "visual_templates": optional category ("", "manuscript", "appendix", "diagnostic", "surface"). scope = "gpcm_capabilities": optional status view ("workflows", "scores", "unavailable"). scopes take additional arguments.

title: Choose an mfrmr output helper by user goal — mfrmr_reporting_and_apa
text: Read Question UseWhen, open help MainFunction. TypicalInput identifies required object NextStep continuation. DecisionBoundary Notes describe limit route; listed function imply every model can use . five default routes choices, required stages. G/D planning uses observed ratings without MFRM fit. Explicit "public" "beginner" retain six-row ordinary RSM/PCM route. scopes select topic output family. Names ending _table, _report, _review _bundle describe role result, interchangeable input classes.

Retain NA/status/reason columns rather replacing unavailable outputs zero. See vignette("mfrmr-reporting--apa", package = "mfrmr") complete fit--manuscript walkthrough.

code: # Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below. # example("plot.mfrm_multivariate_d_study", run.dontrun = TRUE) if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Question: how much would doubling the common tasks change dependability? tasks <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr")) g <- mfrm_g_study(tasks, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL) d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(3, 6, 12)),   weights = c(V = -1, W = 1)) plot(d) # Default: the difference W minus V; higher G/Phi is better. plot(d, type = "sem") # Error in difference-score units; lower is better. plot(d, score = "V") # Inspect an original score separately. # Add intervals for both criteria in the same call. ribbons <- plot(d, score = c("V", "W"), metric = "Phi", reference = 0.8,   intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal") plot_data(ribbons, "intervals") # Saved intervals and their diagnostics. # 0.8 above is an illustrative user criterion, not a recommended cutoff. values <- plot_data(plot(d, draw = FALSE)) values$table # Exact values and availability, rather than reading off a line. if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   p <- as_ggplot(d, type = "sem")   print(p)   # ggplot2::ggsave("d-study-sem.png", p, width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 300) }  # A weight matrix names several choices; explicitly select the plotted one. alternatives <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(3, 6, 12)),   weights = cbind(Equal = c(V = 0.5, W = 0.5), Difference = c(V = -1, W = 1))) plot(alternatives, composite = "Equal") plot(alternatives, composite = "Difference", type = "sem") if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   print(as_ggplot(alternatives, composite = "Equal")) } # Which sources explain error in the difference score? sources <- plot(alternatives, composite = "Difference", type = "error_components") plot_data(sources, "table") # Includes signed cross-score covariance terms. plot_data(sources, "totals") # Error totals, SEM, G/Phi and availability. } # }

text: name Q3-style deliberate. implementation differs Yen's (1984) original Q3 definition two respects together affect threshold interpretation. (1) Standardized vs raw residuals. Yen (1984, eqs. 7-8, p. 127) defines Q3 = cor(d_i, d_j) d_{ik} = u_{ik} - P_hat_{ik} raw residual. mfrmr uses standardized residuals Z = (u - P_hat) / sqrt(Var(u)) diagnose_mfrm() stores. model-based residual scale factors can vary across observations, resulting pair correlations null distribution differ raw-residual Q3. (2) Mean-aggregation. facet paired (e.g. Rater) multiple residual rows per (Person, Level) cell additional facets design (e.g. multiple Criterion rows per Person-Rater cell), standardized residuals first mean-aggregated one value per (Person, Level) cell, Pearson correlation taken mean-aggregated residuals. Yen's original formulation takes correlation directly per-(Person, Item) residuals, without aggregation. Aggregation changes analysis unit persons. correlation based persons observed levels, magnitude null distribution directly comparable raw-row Q3. reasons, treat values returned screening summary rather direct substitute published Q3 thresholds. formal raw-residual Q3 procedure require separately implemented validated design-specific bootstrap; mfrmr currently provide procedure.
